claim: TVC and aero-control actuation is the actuation class spanning engine gimbaling and grid-fin/reentry control on reusable boosters; mapped under the recovery/reentry control parent as the actuation merchant tier.
context: Falcon 9 grid-fin actuation is hydraulic and SpaceX-built; this sub-node carries the merchant actuator tier that the broader launch industry buys. Component-to-parent structural link.

claim: Engine thrust-vector-control actuators gimbal the Merlin engines for steering; on Merlin this is a captive hydraulic system driven by RP-1 turbopump pressure.
context: Captive on SpaceX; sub-node exists to map the merchant TVC-actuator tier serving the wider reusable-launch industry.

claim: The inner 13 Raptor engines on Super Heavy gimbal via thrust-vector-control actuators (switched from hydraulic to in-house electric after Starship flight 1); the outer 20 are fixed.
context: Captive electric actuation on SpaceX; merchant tier mapped for the industry.

claim: Cryogenic propellant/pressurant and pneumatic control valves regulate methane/LOX flow and engine sequencing on the Raptor full-flow staged-combustion engine.
context: SpaceX builds much of its own valve set; this sub-node carries the merchant valve tier (Moog/Woodward/Parker/Eaton) the broader industry uses.

claim: Igniters light the Raptor main chamber and preburners; SpaceX uses an in-house spark/torch ignition system.
context: Documented as genuinely captive — no public merchant igniter supplier to SpaceX found in round 1.

claim: Precision turbopump/gimbal/cryogenic bearings are inspected and life-limited as part of engine reuse; the merchant bearing tier (RBC/Schaeffler/SKF) serves launch-vehicle bearing needs.
context: Turbopump-internal bearings on SpaceX engines are not publicly sourced; merchant tier mapped at industry altitude.

claim: Metal additive-manufacturing machines produce engine hot-section and turbopump parts whose reuse is inspected; SpaceX prints engine parts on Velo3D Sapphire systems.
context: Structural link of the AM-machine merchant component to the engine-reuse/turbopump parent.

claim: Raptor engine components (injectors, manifolds) are additively manufactured on metal LPBF/DMLS machines.
context: Raptor is the highest-AM-content SpaceX engine; merchant AM-machine tier mapped here.

claim: Metal AM powders and specialty-alloy feedstock are the input material for additively manufactured engine parts subject to reuse inspection.
context: GRCop copper-liner alloy is NASA-developed and largely captive at SpaceX; merchant powder tier mapped for the broader industry.

claim: Moog designs and manufactures launch-vehicle thrust-vector-control actuators (electromechanical/electrohydraulic/electrohydrostatic); flight-proven on ULA Vulcan first stage (Jan 2024 inaugural launch), Antares, Centaur and Ares.
context: manufactured_by is asserted for Moog's actual TVC actuators on non-SpaceX programs (Vulcan/Antares/Centaur/Ares). NOT a claim that Moog supplies SpaceX engine actuators (SpaceX TVC is captive). Merchant-tier-to-industry link.

claim: Moog manufactures cryogenic-compatible propellant and pressurant control valves (ball, poppet, pilot-operated) for launch-vehicle engines.
context: manufactured_by for Moog's launch-vehicle engine control valves as a product line; industry altitude, not a SpaceX-specific supply claim.

claim: Woodward manufactures launch-vehicle main-engine controls, thrust-vector-control actuation, flight-control actuation, control valves and servo valves.
context: manufactured_by for Woodward's launch-vehicle actuation product line; industry altitude (Woodward Space & Defense). Not a confirmed SpaceX engine-core supply.

claim: Woodward manufactures control valves and servo valves for launch vehicles.
context: manufactured_by for Woodward's launch-vehicle valve product line.

claim: Parker Aerospace manufactures engine fuel/fluid systems and aerospace valves for missiles, rockets and launch vehicles (e.g. NASA SLS and Orion; historical Space Shuttle / Apollo propellant-feed valves).
context: manufactured_by for Parker's launch-vehicle fluid-systems/valve product line; SLS/Orion named. Industry altitude, not a SpaceX-specific supply claim.

claim: Eaton supplies space propulsion fluid hardware — propellant storage tanks, valves, regulators and feed systems — for spacecraft propulsion (e.g. MDA AURORA satellite propellant tanks, 2024); also aerospace fuel-conveyance and hydraulic pumps.
context: reported_capable_supplier (not manufactured_by): the fetched verbatim is a satellite propulsion-tank selection, not a confirmed launch-vehicle valve supply to a reusable booster. Eaton's launch-vehicle hydraulics history is real but the round-1 fetched quote is satellite-leaning. Honest altitude.

claim: Velo3D manufactures the Sapphire metal laser-powder-bed-fusion machines that SpaceX uses to produce rocket-engine parts including Raptor components; SpaceX signed a Sept-2024 licensing agreement (USD 5M technology + USD 3M engineering).
context: manufactured_by for Velo3D's metal-AM machines; this is the one component where a SpaceX-specific merchant relationship is publicly confirmed (machine supplier, not engine-part maker).

claim: EOS supplies industrial DMLS (laser powder-bed-fusion) machines used to additively manufacture rocket-engine parts (injector heads, copper-alloy combustion chambers) across the launch industry (ArianeGroup, Launcher, RUAG, Airbus D&S).
context: reported_capable_supplier: EOS machines are widely used for rocket-engine AM, but EOS's direct use at SpaceX is not publicly confirmed — industry-capability altitude, not manufactured_by for SpaceX engines.

claim: Nikon SLM Solutions supplies metal LPBF (Selective Laser Melting) machines used to additively manufacture reusable-rocket-engine parts, including full-flow-staged-combustion injector heads and Inconel-718 thrust chambers with integrated cooling channels (Rocket Lab MoU; LEAP 71; university reusable engines).
context: reported_capable_supplier: confirmed for the reusable-rocket-engine industry (Raptor-class FFSC cycle) but not for SpaceX specifically — industry-capability altitude.

claim: Carpenter Additive (Carpenter Technology) supplies iron-, nickel-, cobalt- and titanium-based aerospace alloy metal powders for additive manufacturing of engine and propulsion parts.
context: reported_capable_supplier: merchant aerospace AM-powder maker; SpaceX-specific feedstock supply not confirmed and SpaceX's GRCop copper liner is largely captive. Industry-capability altitude.

claim: ATI supplies titanium and nickel-/cobalt-based superalloy mill products and metal powders (Ti, Ti-aluminides, Ni/Co superalloys) for aerospace engines and additive manufacturing.
context: reported_capable_supplier: merchant Ti + superalloy powder/mill-product maker for aerospace engines; SpaceX-specific supply not confirmed. Industry-capability altitude.

claim: RBC Bearings manufactures FibriloidCR cryogenic self-lubricating spherical bearings/rod ends that are tested and flight-proven for Space Launch Vehicle and satellite applications (-320 degF to +450 degF), plus gimbal assemblies for rocket thrust-vector functions.
context: manufactured_by for RBC's flight-proven launch-vehicle bearing product line (FibriloidCR); a named, launch-specific merchant product. Not asserted as a SpaceX-specific supply.

claim: Schaeffler is a major precision rolling-element bearing manufacturer whose product range covers high-speed and special-environment bearings applicable to turbomachinery/gimbal mechanisms.
context: reported_capable_supplier: reused cross-domain bearing major; specific launch-engine turbopump bearing role is qualitative, not a confirmed SpaceX supply. Industry-capability altitude.

claim: SKF is a major precision bearing manufacturer with aerospace and special-environment bearing lines applicable to launch-vehicle turbomachinery and mechanisms.
context: reported_capable_supplier: reused cross-domain bearing major; specific launch-engine role is qualitative, not a confirmed SpaceX supply. Industry-capability altitude.

claim: The Falcon 9 aluminum-lithium tank structure requires aerospace aluminum-lithium plate/sheet as its base material input.

Constellium manufactures aerospace aluminum-lithium (Airware) plate/sheet for launch-vehicle structures and publicly supplies it to Blue Origin's New Glenn; merchant Al-Li exposure, not a confirmed Falcon 9 BOM claim.
Kaiser Aluminum is a leading aerospace/high-strength aluminum plate producer and a capable second-source for aerospace aluminum plate; not confirmed as an Al-Li launch-tank supplier.
Arconic is a major aerospace rolled-aluminum plate/sheet producer and capable supplier in the aero-aluminum tier; not confirmed as an Al-Li launch-tank supplier.
Falcon 9 titanium grid fins require aerospace mill titanium stock as their base material.
Falcon 9 grid fins require a large single-piece titanium casting/forging process.
Aerospace mill titanium is melted from titanium sponge feedstock (upstream tier).
ATI Inc. melts and mills aerospace/defense-grade titanium products; principal Western merchant melter. Merchant tier exposure, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.
TIMET (a PCC company) produces titanium ingot and mill products and is the largest titanium melter in North America. Merchant tier exposure, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.

VSMPO-AVISMA is the world's largest aerospace mill-titanium producer (historically dominant to Boeing/Airbus) and the export-control corner of this tier; recorded as the concentration risk, not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.
Osaka Titanium Technologies produces titanium sponge and is the world's second-largest sponge producer; core merchant upstream source. Not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.
Toho Titanium produces titanium sponge as one of Japan's two sponge producers; core merchant upstream source. Not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.
TIMET (a PCC company) is the largest titanium sponge producer in North America and operated the last large U.S. sponge plant (idled 2020). Upstream merchant source; not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.

Howmet Aerospace produces large titanium forgings, extrusions and investment castings and is a capable supplier of large aerospace titanium parts; capability exposure, not a confirmed grid-fin supplier (the grid-fin casting is SpaceX-captive).

Precision Castparts produces large aerospace titanium forgings and investment castings and is a capable supplier of large aerospace titanium parts; capability exposure, not a confirmed grid-fin supplier (the grid-fin casting is SpaceX-captive).

Howmet Aerospace is one of the two dominant aerospace investment-casting/forging producers, making >90% of structural and rotating aero-engine component types. Merchant tier exposure, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.
Precision Castparts is one of the two dominant aerospace investment-casting/forging producers in a near-duopoly with Howmet. Merchant tier exposure, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.
Arconic is part of the historic aerospace castings/structures duopoly lineage and a capable supplier of aero structural parts; capability exposure, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM claim.

Outokumpu is reported to supply stainless steel to SpaceX for Starship; merchant 300-series stainless exposure. 304L is a near-commodity grade with many qualified mills, so this is illustrative not sole-source.
Strategic rad-hard processors/FPGAs/memory are the concentrated-supply component within fault-tolerant launch/space avionics.
COTS-upscreened, triple-redundant silicon is the commodity path Falcon-class ascent avionics uses for radiation tolerance, distinct from strategic rad-hard.
Space-grade IMU / inertial reference / GNSS feeds the fault-tolerant GNC loop.
Star trackers provide stellar attitude reference within the GNC sensor suite.
Space-grade connectors and flight harness interconnect the avionics on the reusable launch stack.
Safe-and-arm / ordnance hardware is the energetic component the autonomous flight-safety system commands.
BAE Systems is the heritage leader in strategic rad-hard space processors (RAD750 150nm, RAD5545 45nm); long-standing go-to in high-reliability radiation-hardened space computing.
context: Capability/heritage supplier to the broad reusable-launch + space industry; not asserted as a confirmed SpaceX Falcon BOM item.

claim: Frontgrade Technologies is the self-described largest provider of analog and radiation-hardened electronics (rad-hard FPGAs, memory, microprocessors, processing subsystems).
context: Capability supplier; private (Veritas Capital).

claim: Microchip RTG4 / RT PolarFire are space-qualified rad-tolerant FPGAs; one of the two dominant space-FPGA suppliers.
context: Capability supplier of merchant space-grade FPGAs.

claim: AMD (Xilinx) space-grade XQR Kintex UltraScale and XQR Versal adaptive SoCs are the other dominant merchant space-FPGA line.
context: Capability supplier of merchant space-grade FPGAs/adaptive SoCs.

claim: SkyWater is a DMEA Trusted Foundry funded by DoD ($170M + $99M) to broaden onshore strategic rad-hard (RH90) production capacity.
context: Foundry-capacity provider for the strategic rad-hard corner, not a merchant chip-line seller; from .eval dev set.

claim: Honeywell MIMU (ring-laser-gyro inertial reference) serves commercial and military satellite and launch-vehicle programs; one of two dominant space-IMU houses.
context: Capability supplier; dominant space-grade IMU house.

claim: Northrop Grumman SIRU/HRG inertial reference has 50M on-orbit hours with zero mission failures aboard 200+ spacecraft; the other dominant space-IMU/gyro house.
context: Capability supplier; dominant space-grade inertial house.

claim: Sodern is the self-described world leader in star trackers (Hydra, Auriga) with extensive flight heritage.
context: Market-leading merchant star-tracker supplier.

claim: Jena-Optronik ASTRO APS is the world's most successful and extensively used high-reliability satellite attitude-orbit-control sensor; second established European star-tracker house.
context: Capability supplier; second established star-tracker house.

claim: BAE Systems (former Ball Aerospace) CT-2020 is a radiation-hardened star tracker for spacecraft attitude determination across orbital regimes.
context: Third established star-tracker supplier; Ball Aerospace acquired by BAE in 2024.

claim: Glenair delivers launch-vehicle avionics interconnect systems; its Mighty Mouse is the de facto high-performance connector solution on hundreds of mission-critical applications.
context: Concentrated launch-harness interconnect supplier; private.

claim: TE Connectivity DEUTSCH DBAS connectors are space-qualified for high-temperature, cryogenic, pyrotechnic, and radiation-exposed launch/space environments.
context: Second-source launch-harness interconnect supplier.

claim: Amphenol space-qualified connectors (VITA 78 SpaceVPX) are tested for radiation, extreme temperature, and vibration and meet NASA/ESA outgassing requirements.
context: Third-source launch/space interconnect supplier.

claim: PacSci EMC is the established supplier of safe-and-arm / flight-termination ordnance for U.S. launch vehicles.
context: Concentrated FTS/ordnance corner; subsidiary of Fortive (FTV).

claim: Moog precision motion-control systems control launch vehicles, satellites, and space vehicles (control-surface / actuation electronics and space-grade processing boards).
context: Capability supplier of actuation electronics / control systems; not asserted as a confirmed SpaceX item.

claim: Mercury Systems builds space-qualified FPGA processing boards (incl. first board powered by AMD Xilinx Versal), integrating merchant rad-tolerant silicon into flight subsystems.
context: Board-level integrator of merchant rad-tolerant FPGAs, not a chip maker.

claim: Falcon 9 payload fairings (and other launch-vehicle composite structures) are built from aerospace carbon-fiber composite; the fiber+resin material is the merchant tier while fairing lay-up/cure is captive at SpaceX.

COPVs storing high-pressure helium sit inside the propellant tankage and pressurize the tanks as propellant is consumed; the pressurant-vessel sub-component hangs off the tank/airframe structure module.
COPV overwrap is aerospace carbon-fiber composite over a metal/polymer liner, tying the pressurant vessel back to the same merchant carbon-fiber material tier.
Toray is the world's largest carbon fiber producer and supplies aerospace-grade intermediate-/high-modulus fiber used in aircraft primary structure and the launch-vehicle composite material tier.
Hexcel HexTow carbon fiber and HexPly prepreg are preferred aerospace primary-structure materials (787, A350 XWB, JSF); a merchant carbon-fiber + prepreg supplier in this tier.
Teijin Carbon's Tenax intermediate-modulus carbon fiber is aerospace-qualified (NCAMP with Syensqo resin; Collins Aerospace) — a merchant supplier in the aerospace carbon-fiber tier.

Mitsubishi Chemical Pyrofil PAN carbon fiber and Newport composites are used in aircraft, missile, rocket and satellite structural parts — a merchant supplier in the aerospace carbon-fiber tier, expanding capacity 2025-2027.

Syensqo (legacy Solvay/Cytec composites) supplies aerospace-qualified epoxy resin systems and prepregs (Prism EP2400, NCAMP-qualified) plus carbon fiber — the resin/matrix half of the merchant carbon-composite material tier.
SpaceX builds its own COPVs in-house (captive) for Falcon 9 helium pressurant storage.
Infinite Composites makes COPVs / linerless CPVs for pressurant and propellant tanks in launch vehicles and spacecraft — merchant supplier to the wider industry (SpaceX COPV is captive).
Steelhead Composites makes COPVs integrated into launch-vehicle propulsion systems and spacecraft propulsion tanks — merchant supplier to the wider industry.
HyPerComp Engineering develops/qualifies/produces COPVs used in space launch vehicles; Type IV COPV co-developed with Hexcel HexTow IM11-R fiber — merchant supplier to the wider industry.
GD-OTS Lincoln Operations is design authority for NASA SLS Core/Upper Stage COPVs and satellite propulsion COPVs — merchant supplier to the wider launch/space industry (not SpaceX, which is captive).
Methalox ground propellant operations require merchant helium for pressurizing ground/flight fluid systems and purging propellant lines.
The methane/oxygen ground propellant system requires merchant liquid oxygen as oxidizer feedstock for tank-farm loading.
The methane/oxygen ground propellant system requires rocket-grade liquid methane as the methalox fuel.

Air Products holds NASA's sole-source liquid-helium supply contract (33M liters, ~$1.07B) for Kennedy Space Center / Cape Canaveral launch operations, and is a leading helium supplier to the space-launch industry. NASA-named contract, not a SpaceX-specific contract.

Nippon Sanso/Matheson is one of only a handful of global helium producers/suppliers with owned source rights and long-term supply contracts; modeled as capable merchant helium supply, not a confirmed launch-operator contract.

Messer owns and operates the US Federal Helium System (Cliffside crude-helium source and pipeline) acquired from the BLM in June 2024, a major domestic crude-helium source feeding the merchant helium network. Strategic upstream helium position, not a confirmed launch-operator contract.
Air Liquide supplies helium that is indispensable for pressurization, cool-down and cleaning of launch vehicles; modeled as capable merchant helium supply within the industrial-gas oligopoly.

Linde is SpaceX's main industrial-gas supplier of liquid oxygen and nitrogen, building/owning/operating a dedicated air-separation unit at Brownsville, Texas for SpaceX Starbase and supplying a 'major space launch company' in Florida from its Mims air-separation plant.

Air Liquide supplies liquid oxygen (and nitrogen/helium) for launch vehicles and has a long history supporting Kennedy Space Center launches; modeled as a supplemental/capable LOX supplier alongside Linde.
Air Products is a big-five industrial-gas producer of liquid oxygen via air separation; modeled as a capable merchant LOX supplier, not a confirmed launch-operator LOX contract.
PICA-class ablative material is the heritage ablative branch of reusable/entry thermal protection, parent to the heat-shield tile system module.
The rayon/Lyocell carbon precursor is carbonized into the FiberForm preform that forms the PICA-class ablator.
The carbon FiberForm preform is the rigid matrix impregnated with phenolic to make a PICA-class ablator.
FiberForm preform is manufactured by carbonizing the rayon/Lyocell cellulosic precursor.
Rigid silica/ceramic reusable surface-insulation tile is the reusable-tile material of the heat-shield tile system.
RTV silicone adhesive + Nomex-felt strain-isolator pad are the bonding-material inputs to the tile bonding/inspection process.
Lenzing AG (LENZING Lyocell) supplies the domestic Lyocell carbon precursor used in NASA's PICA-D heatshields.
context: Lyocell low alkaline-metal content makes it suitable as the carbon-fiber precursor; PICA-D is the NASA domestic replacement for the discontinued rayon precursor.

claim: SNIACE was NASA's qualified (non-domestic) rayon precursor supplier for PICA before it ceased production.
context: Heritage sole-qualified rayon precursor; cessation is the documented chokepoint that forced the Lyocell substitution.

claim: Fiber Materials Inc (FMI) manufactures the low-density carbon FiberForm preform used in PICA-class ablators.
context: NASA Ames upgraded FMI facilities to make aerospace-grade FiberForm from the Lyocell precursor (PICA-D).

claim: Lockheed Missiles & Space (Lockheed Martin) developed/manufactured the Shuttle LI-900/LI-2200 reusable silica tiles — heritage maker of reusable ceramic TPS tiles.
context: Heritage/industry reference for the reusable-tile tier; NOT a verified Starship supplier (Starship tiles are captive).

claim: SpaceX manufactures Starship's hexagonal silica ceramic heat-shield tiles in-house (captive) at its tile 'bakery' on Roberts Road.
context: Captive production; no public merchant silica tile supplier is named for Starship.

claim: Momentive Performance Materials supplies RTV silicones for aerospace thermal-protection systems (heritage RTV-560-class tile-bonding adhesive).
context: Industry RTV-adhesive tier; NOT a verified Starship bonding supplier (Starship tile attach is captive).

claim: DuPont's Nomex aramid felt is the heritage strain-isolator-pad (SIP) material between rigid TPS tiles and the airframe.
context: Industry SIP material; NOT a verified Starship supplier.
